newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Force NZ electricity firms to compete, says Labour.
newsitem.headline: Force NZ electricity firms to compete, says Labour.

text.p: The Labour Party on Tuesday called on the government to take regulatory action to ensure competition in the electricity industry.
The party's energy spokesman, Pete Hodgson, accused Energy Minister Max Bradford and SOE Minister Jenny Shipley of "speaking sternly but carrying a non-existent stick".

"We have heard it all before. For three years the previous Minister of Energy, Doug Kidd, told electricity companies that their fixed prices were too high, and that he might have to act," Hodgson said.

"It made no difference ... now Mr Bradford and Mrs Shipley have wagged their fingers at the industry but, after the industry pays careful and courteous attention to the ministers, it is still business as usual and still more price hikes."

Hodgson said that years after deregulation there were still high fixed prices, virtually no separation of line and energy companies, and "hand-wringing allocations of blame every time the price moves up".
"It is absolutely clear that competition is a myth not a reality," he said.
Fixed charges should be outlawed and line and energy companies should be separated.
"The tut-tutting and finger wagging must stop. Too many little people are losing too much money to a large and still complacent industry," Hodgson said.
